newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods quits Freeman mail order talks.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods quits Freeman mail order talks.

text.p: British retail to football pools company Littlewoods Group on Friday pulled out of talks to buy the Freemans mail order business of Sears Plc and said it would only return if other potential buyers were excluded.
"We are still very interested in talking to them about Freemans but only on an exclusive basis," a spokeswoman for Littlewoods, Britain's largest private company, said.
Sears, which had hoped to sell Freemans for 395 million pounds ($635 million), said it had received a number of approaches from firms interested in buying the business.
The two companies agreed the deal in January but the British government referred it to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) for competitions review.
The deal would have given Littlewoods around 25 percent of the British mail order market, just enough to justify a competiton inquiry.
"Sears wanted to be 100 percent certain of a sale and although it was on to a sure-fire deal with Littlewoods there was some doubt over the MMC inquiry," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
The MMC will be talking to both parties to clarify whether both sides have abandoned the deal and then could call off the inquiry.
A spokeswoman for Sears said the company could not give exclusivity to Littlewoods after it had received other offers and wanted to consider the best in the interests of shareholders.
"We would prefer not to go (back) on to an exclusive basis," she said. She declined to give details of the other approaches, however.
Some analysts suggested that Littlewoods and Sears might have received indications that the MMC was unlikely to approve the deal.
The breakdown of talks could present a further headache for Sears chief executive Liam Strong, who has been under heavy fire from shareholders unhappy with his running of the business.

Sears issued a profits warning in January after a disappointing Christmas, and Strong's plans to sell off the group's loss-making shoe business foundered last year when the buyer, privately-owned Facia, collapsed.
"It's not bad news for Sears, there should be other buyers, but it is bad news for Liam Strong," the analyst said.
Analysts said home shopping company N. Brown , which currently has around 3.5 percent of the market, could be interested in buying Freemans.
But they added that N. Brown, which was not available for comment, might have to make a rights issue to fund such an acquisition.
Sears had planned to mollify shareholders with a 410 million pound payout if the Littlewoods deal went through and this might now be under pressure, analysts said.
Littlewoods said that it would now "accelerate our plans for developing our direct offers," including direct home shopping and niche catalogues.
"With or without Freemans, Littlewoods is a key player in home shopping and is a leading business with excellent prospects," the company added.
Sears shares closed down 0.25 pence at 81.75 pence. ($ = 0.622 British Pounds)
